summary: Sheriff's deputies booked a 36-year-old man on drug trafficking and firearm charges and a 23-year-old man on a rape charge, and Daphne police arrested eight people on prostitution and solicitation charges on Friday. The jail roster showed 26 criminal bookings dated Nov. 6 and one so far on Nov. 7.

entries.title: Drug trafficking arrest: Arvia Lloyd Allen
body: Sheriff's deputies arrested Arvia Lloyd Allen, 36, at 1:59 a.m. Friday, Nov. 6, according to the jail roster. He was in custody when the roster was read early Saturday.

He was booked on charges of drug trafficking — possessing or selling drugs in an amount the law treats as trafficking — and of being a drunk or drug addict in possession of a firearm, along with possession of dangerous drugs, marijuana possession and drug paraphernalia. The roster lists six charges in all. The sheriff's office had not posted a release about the arrest when its page was checked.

entries.title: Rape arrest: Dylan Dwayne Harbison
body: Sheriff's deputies arrested Dylan Dwayne Harbison, 23, at 3:36 p.m. Thursday, Nov. 5, according to the jail roster, which shows him booked into the jail on Friday, Nov. 6. He was in custody when the roster was read early Saturday.

He was booked on a charge the jail lists as rape by force, and on a charge of sexual contact without consent or with a child aged 12 to 16. The sheriff's office had not posted a release about the arrest when its page was checked.

entries.title: Elder abuse arrests: Brandon James Ingle, Edward Arley Hale
body: Sheriff's deputies arrested Brandon James Ingle, 38, at 8:35 a.m. Friday, Nov. 6, and Edward Arley Hale, 67, at 8:42 a.m., according to the jail roster. Both were in custody when the roster was read early Saturday.

Each was booked on a charge of second-degree elder abuse and neglect — abusing or neglecting a person aged 60 or older. The roster does not say whether the two arrests are connected, and the sheriff's office had not posted a release when its page was checked.

entries.title: Stolen-property and altered-firearm arrest: Damon Curtis Chisholm
body: Sheriff's deputies arrested Damon Curtis Chisholm, 51, at 2:55 p.m. Friday, Nov. 6, according to the jail roster. He was in custody when the roster was read early Saturday.
He was booked on charges of buying or receiving stolen property, and of altering a firearm's identification or possessing an altered firearm — a gun with its serial number removed or changed.

entries.title: Drunk-driving arrests: Robert Glen Coats, Travis Jefferey Moran
body: Sheriff's deputies arrested Robert Glen Coats, 68, at 4 p.m. Thursday, Nov. 5, on a charge the jail lists as driving under the influence of alcohol with three or more prior convictions, according to the jail roster. He was booked Friday and was in custody when the roster was read early Saturday.
State troopers arrested Travis Jefferey Moran, 38, at 9:02 a.m. Nov. 5 on a charge of driving under the influence of alcohol. He was booked and released Friday, Nov. 6, according to the roster.

entries.title: Attempting-to-elude arrests: Trevor O'Neal Lochrico, Justin Taylor Covington
body: Sheriff's deputies arrested Trevor O'Neal Lochrico, 36, at 1:21 p.m. Thursday, Nov. 5, on two counts of shoplifting and a charge of attempting to elude police — fleeing from an officer who signals a stop — according to the jail roster.

Deputies arrested Justin Taylor Covington, 29, at 1 p.m. Friday, Nov. 6, on a charge of attempting to elude police. Both were booked Nov. 6 and were in custody when the roster was read early Saturday.

entries.title: Card fraud arrest: Danielle Zaneta Kennedy
body: Sheriff's deputies arrested Danielle Zaneta Kennedy, 41, at 4:50 p.m. Friday, Nov. 6, according to the jail roster. She was in custody when the roster was read early Saturday.
She was booked on three counts of illegal possession or use of a credit or debit card — having or using someone else's card without permission.

entries.title: Family-harassment arrest: Julian Morales
body: Sheriff's deputies arrested Julian Morales, 22, at 11:20 a.m. Friday, Nov. 6, according to the jail roster. He was in custody when the roster was read early Saturday.
He was booked on a charge of harassment of a family member — threatening, striking or alarming a household member.

entries.title: Bay Minette arrests: Caitlin Carol Reed, Ashton Harold Enrico Bradley, Madison Taylor Cubbage
body: Bay Minette police arrested Caitlin Carol Reed, 27, at 3:15 p.m. Friday, Nov. 6, according to the jail roster. She was booked on charges including drug paraphernalia, tampering with physical evidence, promoting prison contraband (drugs) — bringing drugs into a jail — harassment of a family member and failure to appear; the roster lists seven charges in all.

Bay Minette police also arrested Ashton Harold Enrico Bradley, 36, at 8:30 a.m. Nov. 6 on a charge of second-degree marijuana possession; he was released the same day. Madison Taylor Cubbage, 27, booked Nov. 6 with an arrest stamp of 1:48 a.m. Saturday, Nov. 7, faces an alias writ of arrest and failure-to-appear warrants, 14 charges in all. Reed and Cubbage were in custody when the roster was read.

entries.title: Daphne prostitution arrests: eight charged Nov. 6
body: Daphne police arrested five men on charges of solicitation for prostitution between 11:03 a.m. and 3:10 p.m. Friday, Nov. 6, all on Woodrow Lane, according to the department's arrest log: Jonathan Kirk Fender, Jayden Alexander Kelley, Jocquez Tyree Dixon, Jordan Ray Phillips and Joseph Dewayne Bates.

Between 10:48 and 11:15 p.m. the same night, officers arrested Carlos Maurice Byther, Carlton De'aundre Eonte Lee and Juan Vellejo on charges of prostitution at the Microtel on U.S. 98, the log shows. Daphne police had not posted a release about the arrests when the department's page was checked.

entries.title: Federal sentences, bank fraud and identity theft: Vernon A. McCreath, Mikhail C. McCreath
body: Vernon A. McCreath, 39, of Jersey City, New Jersey, was sentenced to 192 months and Mikhail C. McCreath, 35, of Miami, to 140 months in federal prison for a nationwide bank fraud and identity theft scheme, the U.S. Attorney's Office for the Southern District of Alabama announced Nov. 6. Both had pleaded guilty.

According to the release, the scheme ran from 2015 to 2025, used stolen mail, counterfeit checks and stolen identities, and passed instruments at banks in the Southern District of Alabama, among other places. The Baldwin County Sheriff's Office was among the agencies the release says substantially assisted the investigation.
